evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: MaizeMate is our WhatsApp AI assistant that answers agronomy questions for smallholder maize farmers in western Kenya. The goal is better yields through timely top-dressing. We've piloted with about 1,400 farmers through two cooperatives. Last quarter we benchmarked answers against an agronomist-written test set and 88% were rated acceptable. Usage is spiky: a lot of farmers ask one question and never come back. Our funder wants to discuss an RCT at the October board meeting and we need to decide what to propose. Which evaluation should we run next?
evals.expected_output: A recommendation in the output template that says to evaluate use of the product now and that the RCT is premature, with the evidence behind each stage's verdict.
assertions: Makes one recommendation, and it is to evaluate engagement or retention now, not to run the RCT.
Gives all four stages a verdict beside named evidence or 'none supplied', citing the 88% test-set result for the model stage and the one-question drop-off for the product stage.
Explains why a yield trial now would be hard to interpret, in words the team could give the funder.
Lists at least one thing to build now, such as version tags, a holdout group, or randomized rollout.
Says what evidence would change the recommendation.
Ends with two or three next moves, each with its reason, and questions the user could ask next, with no single instruction.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: Our funder wants us to run an RCT on our chatbot next year. Should we?
evals.expected_output: The skill asks what the product does, what evidence exists so far, and what decision the answer informs, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks what the product does, for whom, or what outcome it is meant to improve.
Asks what has been tested or measured so far.
Does not produce the table of stages.
Does not say yes or no to the RCT.
Says why it needs these answers.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: Our Swahili maternal-health WhatsApp assistant has run for 18 months with about 40,000 users across three counties in Kenya. Model: a weekly test set, including questions it must refuse, passes above 92%, with answers reviewed by midwives. Product: 4-week retention has been stable around 55% for six months. Users: two before-and-after survey rounds showed gains in knowledge of pregnancy danger signs, and an A/B test of proactive reminders raised antenatal clinic bookings by 6 percentage points. The Ministry of Health wants to scale to ten counties next year and a funder has offered to pay for an impact evaluation. What should we evaluate next?
evals.expected_output: The skill recommends an impact evaluation now, citing the evidence at the first three stages, and tells the user to bring in an independent evaluator and a clinical expert.
assertions: Recommends an impact evaluation as the evaluation to run now.
Cites the 92% pass rate, the 55% retention, and the booking or knowledge results as the evidence for the first three stages.
Says the first three stages still need monitoring and are not finished.
Tells the user to bring in an independent evaluator to design the impact evaluation.
Tells the user to involve a clinical or other domain expert because the product gives health advice.
Lists what to build now, such as using the county rollout to create a comparison group.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: We run an SMS vaccination reminder program in two districts: scheduled texts, no AI involved. Which of the four AI evaluation levels should we run next?
evals.expected_output: The skill says the stages assume an AI model in the program, and points to the skill for planning an evaluation.
assertions: Says the program has no AI model, so this skill does not apply.
Names plan-evaluation-design.
Does not produce the table of stages.
